sections.overview: The green bomber worm is a free-swimming deep-sea annelid in the family Acrocirridae.
sections.identification: Its mostly transparent body bears paired branchial sacs that glow green when detached.
sections.habitat: It lives in the deep water column of the northeastern Pacific; records include midwater off California.
sections.diet: Its diet has not been established in the sources consulted.
sections.behavior: When disturbed, it can release glowing branchial sacs. The light may distract predators while it swims away.
sections.reproduction: Its reproductive biology is not described in the sources consulted.
sections.ecology: The detached luminous structures are modified gills and are interpreted as a defensive decoy, not a reproductive release.
sections.conservation: The scientific sources consulted describe its discovery and biology but give no conservation category.
